summary: Ben-Gvir reportedly traveled by police helicopter from a private vacation to official/public appearances and back; separate election-law scrutiny concerned his participation in a police-volunteer/security-squad event.
discovery_sources: Contemporaneous helicopter reporting; Jerusalem Post 2026-08-24; Times of Israel 2026-08-24; Central Elections Committee reporting
resolution_notes: Freshness update adds material exculpatory/procedural context: CEC chair Noam Sohlberg rejected a petition seeking to bar Ben-Gvir from attending and speaking at the police volunteer/security-squad event after Ben-Gvir gave a sworn undertaking not to campaign there. Sohlberg explicitly preserved the ban on campaigning at the event and recommended legal review of the speech. This means attendance/speaking at that event cannot itself be treated as an adverse election-law finding. The separate helicopter use still lacks a sufficiently complete primary authorization/cost/official-response record and no post-event ruling establishing a campaign breach surfaced. Preserve Pending; do not infer illegality or motive.
media_status: No canonical media item while Pending; do not use generic event imagery.
